messages:
ana: Heads up — onboarding quickpack for customer Caspian (LoRA v0.4) surfaced a weird combo failure: numeric grouping breaks + a subtle rerank flip on invoice line extraction. Putting repros here.

 tom: Can you drop the minimal failing case?

 ana: Sure. Two examples from their prompt set: 

 ```
 input: "Line item: 2 x Widget A — $1,200.00 each"
 expected: "2 x Widget A — $1,200.00 each"
 int4-output: "2 x Widget A — 1200.00 dollars each"
 
 input: "Extract the highest invoice line and amount"
 expected-rank: ["Widget A: $1,200.00", "Widget B: $800.00"]
 int4-rank: ["Widget B: $800.00", "Widget A: 1200.00 dollars"]
 ```

 jyoti: Interesting — two related failures: tokenization (comma merging) and a rerank/formatization that prefers verbalized units. Which quant stack?

 ana: GPTQ-4bit with tokenizer v16. We also saw the float fp16 baseline is clean. Quickpack summary: 150 tests total, 5 fails (all numeric grouping/rerank related).

 eval-bot: quick-eval uploaded: s3://redwood-test-results/caspian/3876543210/summary.json  5 failures (numeric-group, rerank-flip)

 tom: If fp16 is clean this strongly points to token merges after quant conversion. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add a routing rule to send requests with invoice-like regex to fp16; 2) add a postprocessing normalization that preserves comma-separated numbers back into local format when entity detected. Both are stopgaps.

 jyoti: For a robust fix we should compare tokenization between fp16 and int4 builds for the failing inputs. I can run token-diff and also inspect the adapter weight stats to ensure LoRA didn't nudge generation probability to verbalized forms.

 ana: Token diffs (excerpt): 

 ```
 tokenized(fp16): ["2"," ","x"," ","Widget"," ","A"," ","—"," ","$","1"," ,","200",".","00"]
 tokenized(int4): ["2"," ","x"," ","Widget"," ","A"," ","—"," ","$","1200.00"]
 ```

 jyoti: Looks like the comma got swallowed into the numeric token in the quantized tokenizer which likely changes the model's surface form distribution (it now emits plain number + unit). I'll try a quick pre-tokenization micro-patch that inserts a zero-width separator between digits and commas before tokenization and run quickpack with that enabled only for the Caspian adapter.

 ops-bot: CI job queued: quickpack/3876543210-diff (matrix: fp16,int4-gptq,int4-awq)  job=223344

 tom: Also worth checking embedding drift for the line items since the rerank flip suggests embeddings or probability mass moved. Can you run a micro-eval that computes cosine similarity for line-item spans between fp16/int4?

 jyoti: On it. Preliminary embed diff: avg cosine(fp16 vs int4) on line-item spans = 0.86 (small drift) but for the failing cases it's 0.72. That's nontrivial. Possibly the token merge changed context window tokenization which impacted KV cache alignment a bit.

 ana: Ok plan: jyoti lands pre-tokenization patch as AWQ/GPTQ gated flag for the adapter, tom wires a routing fallback to fp16 for invoice-like traffic, and I will add the five failing prompts to tests/caspian_invoice_quick.jsonl and tag them blocking. If pre-tokenization + gated deploy fixes both format and rerank, we can remove the fp16 fallback.

 jyoti: PR opened: infra/quant/patches#802  title="pre-tokenize: zero-width-sep between digit and comma for caspian adapter"  diff: small

 ops-bot: PR pipeline passed  canary scheduled: canary/caspian-digitsep @ 2025-05-15T03:00:00Z  pool: dedicated-canary-2

 tom: I'll set route rule: if header x-client-id=caspian and body matches (invoice|line item|total|amount|\$\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+) -> model=base-cascade-fp16 (route-lift for 30m default).

 ana: Added tests and updated quickpack metadata. Also pinged customer success to give a heads up about temporary routing while we verify.

 eval-bot: quickpack run complete for job=223344  result: patched int4 build passes 150/150  artifacts: s3://redwood-test-results/caspian/3876543210/postpatch.json :tada:

 ana: Great. Once canary is stable we'll promote patch to prod and retire the fp16 emergency rule. Thanks team for the quick cycle.
